name: Anastomosing Haemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Anastomosing Haemangioma

criteria.description: Presence of anastomosing, sinusoidal vascular channels lined by bland endothelial cells without significant atypia or mitotic activity
Positive endothelial markers such as CD31, CD34, and ERG confirming vascular origin
Solitary, well-circumscribed lesion typically found incidentally or presenting with localized symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of characteristic vascular architecture with endothelial marker positivity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from angiosarcoma is critical due to benign behavior of anastomosing haemangioma

pathognomonic.notes: Typically found in the kidney or genitourinary tract

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anastomosing sinusoidal vascular channels on histology

common.symptomName: Incidental asymptomatic mass detected on imaging
common.notes: Often discovered during imaging for unrelated reasons
Due to mass effect in renal or retroperitoneal locations
searchTerms: pain in side or stomach area

common.notes: Occasionally present if lesion involves urinary tract

occasional.notes: Rarely palpable depending on size and location

occasional.symptomName: Mild anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
occasional.notes: Uncommon but possible if lesion bleeds

occasional.symptomName: Elevated serum creatinine if renal function impaired

rare.notes: Very rare but potentially serious complication

rare.symptomName: Secondary hypertension due to renal involvement

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of serum creatinine
imaging: Well-circumscribed, hypervascular mass on CT or MRI
No evidence of local invasion or metastasis
other: Histopathology showing anastomosing sinusoidal vascular channels lined by bland endothelial cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD31, CD34, ERG

distinguishingFeatures: Marked cytologic atypia and mitotic activity
Presence of spindle cells and slit-like vascular spaces
Multifocal lesions often involving skin and mucosa

redFlags: Histologic features suggestive of malignancy (atypia, mitoses)
Evidence of local invasion or metastasis on imaging
references: Martinez A et al. Anastomosing hemangioma: a distinctive benign vascular neoplasm. Am J Surg Pathol. 2009.
Fletcher CDM et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone. 4th Edition. 2013.
Kang Y et al. Imaging features of anastomosing hemangioma of the kidney. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 2015.
